title: Search Linear with AI: find the issue you half remember
h1: find a linear issue from the words you remember
description: Find Linear issues by a phrase, title or issue reference with an AI bot. Include archived work when needed and see why team filters need another action.
answer: **stop asking the team who remembers that ticket.** give the bot words from the problem, title or issue reference. it searches linear and brings back matches, including archived work when you ask. use the separate team-listing action when you need one team’s backlog: putting a team, project or person’s name in this search only adds words.

review.by: lead agent, after two independent reviewer passes, against Metal docs and the composio catalog

og_line: the ticket behind a half-remembered phrase.
what:
**dig up the old investigation before repeating it.** this search reads issue titles, descriptions and references. archived work stays out unless you ask for it.

you get 25 matches by default, with up to 50 in a batch. the bot can fetch more. team, project, owner, status and label filters need a different action; use list issues by team for a team’s issues.
uses: **recover a support lead.** find the ticket about a blank screen after sign-in.
**pick up an old investigation.** include archives before reopening the same question.
**prepare for a support call.** collect tickets mentioning the exact error phrase.
**find a half-remembered ticket.** use words from its description.

routine.message:
every monday at 11, search linear for "password reset", including archived issues.

- finish reading available results
- bring the issue titles and references here
- mark archived results separately
- flag loose matches

include the matching phrase beside loose matches. never edit, reopen or create an issue.
routine.needs: linear connected with read only for this bot
routine.output:
password reset matches
web-84: reset link opens a blank page; active
web-19: reset email delay; archived
web-84 is the closest match for the blank-page investigation.

steps: **connect linear with read only.** search needs no write access.
**give it the phrase.** include the error words and say whether archives belong in the results.
**open the closest tickets.** ask the bot to fetch remaining results before calling the list complete.
**schedule a topic worth watching.** pause when the investigation ends.
watch: **a team name is just another word here.** use the separate team-listing action for a team boundary.
**bring the archives into an old-bug search.** ask for them by name so earlier work appears.
**50 is the largest batch.** there may still be more matches to read.

faq.a: **not with this action.** it checks the issue reference, title and description. reading comments takes a separate step.

faq.q: what if i do not know the ticket number?
faq.a: **quote the problem instead.** the bot can show candidates and ask which one you meant.
**no, it only finds them.** archived issues stay as they are.

steps: compare the matching title and description with your problem

mistakes.mistake: adding "ops team" and expecting a team filter
mistakes.fix: that only adds search words. use list issues by team when the team matters.
include archives when you suspect someone solved this before.

items: you need words from a title, description or issue reference
you chose whether to include archives
you are not relying on team, owner, project, status or label filters
you will read the matching issue before using it

tip.text: the exact error message is a better clue than "that bug from last month".
